title: The Great Pyramid of Giza built
summary: The Great Pyramid of Giza built
description: Added from the Generations curriculum import (Taking Africa for Jesus). Dated only by the Generations books cited below; no tier 1–4 chronology covers this event.

sorting_basis.note: PROVISIONAL: no CFAH, Ussher–Jones or Ussher date exists, so the sort uses Generations (Taking Africa for Jesus, PDF p. 19): around 2258 BC. Pending owner decision (open question A8).

chronologies.note: pending CFAH reference (the CFAH series does not cover this period; no tier 1–4 date exists)

chronologies.citation: Taking Africa for Jesus, ch. 2 "Egypt (Part 1)", PDF p. 19 (printed p. 19)
chronologies.note: Date given with the pyramid of Giza.

chronologies.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020), ch. 5 "The Egyptian Empire (2450–332 BC)", PDF p. 119 (printed p. 118)
chronologies.note: "Possible" date. Timeline Review pairs it with an asterisked 2088 BC (the book's Ussher-chronology equivalent). (p. 166, "Cheops").
chronologies.edition_note: 1st ed. (2020); superseded by the 2nd ed. (2024), which prints "1923–1903 BC" (PDF p. 188): 335 years later.

chronologies.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (2nd ed., 2024), ch. 9 "Early Egypt and the Exodus of God's People", PDF p. 188 (printed p. 174)
chronologies.note: Sole reign of Cheops, about 322 years after the Tower of Babel.

chronologies.date: “after him Cheops succeeded to the throne”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 2.124 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 149 (PDF p. 151)
chronologies.note: Cheops follows Rhampsinitus, who followed Proteus (2.121). CONFLICT in sequence: Herodotus puts the pyramid builders after Proteus, the contemporary of the Trojan War (CFAH AP-12, 1184/1183 BC). CFAH-6 places Khufu near Abraham's visit (1921 BC), Generations dates the Great Pyramid about 2258 BC (Taking Africa for Jesus; the provisional sort) and 1923–1903 BC (Preparing, 2nd ed.).

chronologies.date: “The pyramid itself was twenty years in building.”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 2.124 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 149 (PDF p. 151)
chronologies.note: Also ten years for the causeway (2.124).

chronologies.date: “Cheops reigned, the Egyptians said, fifty years”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 2.127 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 150 (PDF p. 152)

chronologies.date: “Thus the affliction of Egypt endured for the space of one hundred and six years”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 2.128 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 151 (PDF p. 153)
chronologies.note: The temples were shut under Cheops and Chephren (50 + 56 = 106). DERIVED (not Herodotus's figure): CFAH-6 uses this figure: "Counting from Abraham’s visit in 1921 BC, the 106 years comes to 1815 BC." Derived by CFAH. CFAH-6 (citing this edition, p. 151) adopts the 106 years.
